title: Backdoor Trigger Sensitivity in Safety-Trained Models: Does Trigger Length Matter?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly informs how safety fine-tuning should be augmented with backdoor-specific detection. If shorter triggers survive better, adversaries will prefer them, changing the threat model. Actionable for supply-chain security.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires inserting backdoors via poisoned SFT data (custom data pipeline), running DPO safety fine-tuning for each trigger length, and measuring survival rates. Multiple training runs with custom data is well beyond beginner scope.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Five trigger lengths times (SFT poisoning + DPO fine-tuning + evaluation) = at least 5 full training cycles. Far too many training runs for 30 hours of beginner effort on medium compute.
